findings.summary: This is the fourth checkpoint in a row where state.json does not say what is true, and the gate written for it (M18.266) was passed over for three feature commits. `updated` is not a clock. 97a5c8c set it to 21:05:00Z, ten minutes after its own landing (20:55:24Z). dddcdb5 then moved it back to 20:57:29Z. 9d405b4 set 22:30:00Z, 55 minutes after it landed (21:35:15Z). 5883d3c moved it back to 22:05:03.802Z. c57b425, 483217b and cdeb16f each change currentTask and close a row, and none of them moves it. blockedReason at HEAD still says 'M18.250-252 wait on it' (the F4 card), but M18.250 and M18.251 are on main. The held gate (6222385) only requires `updated` to be later than HEAD's, and its own review left 'no upper bound on `updated`' open. On this history it would have accepted 97a5c8c's and 9d405b4's future times and then refused the next honest commit, which teaches drivers to write a later fake time.

findings.failure_scenario: M18.266 lands as it is. The next driver whose real time is earlier than a future-dated `updated` on main is refused, and writes a later time to pass, so the clock records whatever passes the gate. Or a replay through land.mjs, which takes upstream's state.json on conflict as these three replays did, is refused at every landing. Either way blockedReason keeps telling the next session that landed rows are blocked.

findings.summary: M18.122 landed with a lost changes-requested review round, which is the ledger gap cp38 F4, cp40 F1, cp41 F1 and cp42 F6 were about. Its message says 'a first pass (changes-requested, restaged before it was recorded), then recorded round 1 changes-requested and round 2 pass', plus a rebind review in round 3. That is four reviews against three digest lines and a cap of 3, with no over-cap mark and no allowance. Its progress entry numbers them r1 changes-requested, r2 changes-requested and r3 pass, while the digest has r2 as pass. M18.268's acceptance covers 'a task commit's message or added progress lines', but check-digest and the commit-msg hook read only the body (namedRoundProblems, messageRoundProblems). Only review.mjs record reads progress hunks, and record is not re-run when land.mjs re-commits. The body's wording ('a first pass') names no rN, so the body check cannot see the round.
findings.evidence: Digest: M18.122 r1 changes-requested (4 findings), r2 pass (2), r3 pass (3). None is over-cap. thresholds.mjs:14 REVIEW_ROUND_CAP 3. Probe at cdeb16f: namedRounds(c57b425's added progress lines, 'M18.122') = {rounds [1,2,3], sentBack [1,2]}, and missingRounds over those three lines = ['round r2 as changes-requested (the text sends it back, no changes-requested line holds it)']. namedRounds(c57b425's body) = {rounds [1,2,3], sentBack [1]} -> []. check-digest --head --full-history passes (310 commits). check-digest.mjs:273-279 passes only `git log -1 --format=%B` to messageRoundProblems. review.mjs:124-133 reviewTexts reads staged progress hunks at record time only.
findings.failure_scenario: A replayed or long-lived row loses a round before recording, or under a reworded message. It passes the cap with no human allowance, and the only text that tells the truth (progress.md) is never checked once the commit exists. The next checkpoint finds it by hand again, as this one did.

questions.coherence: Coherent. M18.265 and M18.268 close cp42's two gate holes in the shapes cp42 asked for, and M18.264 fixes the test at its cause, not its bound. M18.250 -> M18.251 form one design: core writes and validates connectors.json, the sdk reads it with loadPackConnectors, and the studio registers it per document under ADR-0183's embedded-first rule. They share one refusal model with the index (refused file listed, the pack's shapes kept). M18.122 reuses registerSavedShapePacks rather than adding a second registration path. The incoherence is in the record, not the code: state.json's clock and blockedReason (F1), and M18.122's three versions of its own round count (F2).

questions.architecture: Clean. Layering shows 0 violations. core gains connectors in ShapePackDraft and imports parseConnectorDefs and describeOf from within core. The sdk's Pack/PackSpec gain an optional connectors field (sdk.api.md updated, ADR-0017 and ADR-0048 amendments). No dependency was added. connectors.json sits outside the index's category hashes by design (ADR-0048 amendment M18.250), so its integrity rests on the loader's validation rather than the index hash. That is acceptable for declarative types, and worth one line in the amendment if it is not there already.
